claims.text: Formation and retention of a protective oxide above 900 °C are governed by formation of an adherent composite scale containing Cr2O3 and an X-derived oxide.
Si additions promote formation of dense, slow-growing SiO2 that integrates with Cr2O3.
Al additions promote formation of dense, slow-growing Al2O3 that integrates with Cr2O3.
Mn does not form an equivalently protective X-derived oxide in this alloy family.
Mn-containing alloys instead form mixed, fast-growing oxides prone to cracking or spallation.
At high temperature, Cr segregates to the alloy surface and reacts with oxygen.
In Si-containing alloys, Si segregates to the surface and forms SiO2.
In Al-containing alloys, Al segregates to the surface and forms Al2O3.
Intermixing SiO2 or Al2O3 with Cr2O3 produces a dense, adherent scale with a low growth rate.
Mn favors a heterogeneous oxide mixture that grows rapidly.
Rapid growth of the heterogeneous Mn-containing scale creates internal stresses and thermal-expansion mismatches.
Internal stresses and thermal-expansion mismatches cause cracking and spallation of the Mn-containing scale.
Si-containing CrFeCoNiX alloys will form a stable, coherent oxide that resists cracking and spallation.
Al-containing CrFeCoNiX alloys will form a stable, coherent oxide that resists cracking and spallation.
Mn-containing CrFeCoNiX alloys will develop an unstable, spalling oxide scale.
The CrFeCoNi baseline will form an oxide scale of intermediate quality because it lacks a stabilizing X-derived oxide.
The proposed mechanism applies above 900 °C in both single-phase and multiphase metallic solid-solution states.
Oxygen concentration and the concentration of corrosive species can influence the oxidation behavior.
